messages:
marcel: heads-up: i'm seeing ~30 tiny-gang gpu pods stuck PENDING across eu-west1-a/b, all from the same nightly batch job.
anya: ack, can you paste one pod describe?
marcel: sure — main oddity: `NodeAffinity` looks fine but scheduler keeps backoff. kubelet logs show `lease renewal failed` for the gpu-manager and conntrack counters spiking. snippet: ```
W0102 03:12:11.123 kubelet.go:123] lease renew error: timeout
I0102 03:12:11.456 gpu-manager.go:88] orphaned-lease detected for pod gpu-batch-xyz
```
jia: orphaned-lease? that smells like our lease controller race introduced in the AZ-label rollout. we had a partial label flip earlier today.
marcel: yeah nodes in eu-west1-b have the new `tile-shelf` label, eu-west1-a not yet; scheduler's topology aware binpacking seems to prefer labeled nodes so pods land in a tight subset and then get queued because the warm-pool nodes in that subset hit conntrack+nic soft limit.
sre-bot: :rotating_light: detected spike: conntrack_entries > 95% on warmpool-nodes-eu-west1b-*. autoscaler paused new allocations.
anya: so two compounding things: label skew -> affinity concentrating tiny gangs -> warm pool NIC/conntrack saturation -> lease refresh failures -> orphaned leases -> scheduler thinks slot occupied?
devops: quick mitigation: can we 1) temporarily disable the tile-shelf soft-affinity for the nightly job, or 2) expand warm pool on eu-west1-a so load evens out?
marcel: tried disabling affinity on a single job run with `spec.affinity.podAntiAffinity` -> slight improvement but doesn't clear existing orphaned leases.
sam: for orphaned leases we can force cleanup with our lease-rectifier: `kubectl exec -n infra lease-rectifier -- /bin/rectify --namespace=gpu-batch --selector=job=nightly` — will that cause churn?
jia: safe-ish; it will delete stale lease objects older than 30s and trigger kube-scheduler resync. Still want to be careful during peak.
anya: short plan: (1) run lease-rectifier in dry-run to list orphans, (2) scale warm pool +1 in eu-west1-a to pull backlog, (3) roll node label change to remaining nodes in eu-west1-a to remove parity skew, (4) open a quick PR to add conntrack guardrail on warm-pool autoscaling and increase node sysctl `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` for GPU nodes.
marcel: running dry-run now. output: `found 28 orphaned leases for selector job=nightly; oldest 9m; nodes referenced: warmpool-eu-west1b-*(24), warmpool-eu-west1a-*(4)`
sam: i'll bump warmpool in eu-west1-a by 3 now.
sre-bot: action: warmpool-scale request submitted (change_id=wp-1623).
marcel: doing `kubectl exec lease-rectifier -- --dry-run --selector=job=nightly` shows which leases map to pods that no longer exist. ok to delete?
jia: yes, safe to delete the ones where pod uid not present. proceed but throttled to 5/s.
anya: i'll open the PR for conntrack defaults: increase nf_conntrack_max from 262144 -> 524288 for `gpu-type` nodepool and add kubelet eviction logging when conntrack > 80%. link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/conntrack-guard
devops: also recommend we add scheduler soft-affinity decay window — if label skew caused >60% of a job's pods to target one topo domain, gradually relax affinity for new pods for 10m. i'll draft an experiment.
marcel: after rectifier deletes 20 leases and warmpool bump, 12 pods moved into Running, 16 still pending mostly eu-west1b.
sam: I'll reroute a couple jobs to eu-west1-a by setting nodeSelector on the job for now. low-risk.
anya: follow-up tickets: INFRA-7392 (conntrack sysctl bump + cluster config), INFRA-7393 (scheduler soft-affinity decay probe), INFRA-7394 (lease-controller retry backoff fix).
jia: long-term: we should stop coupling warm-pool scaling to single-label heuristics; prefer capacity-aware spreading across AZs. also re-evaluate our lease lifecycle: make it resilient to short conntrack blips.
marcel: agreed. for now we recovered ~70% of stuck pods, will monitor next 2 hours and revert manual nodeSelectors after label rollout completes. thanks all :thumbsup:
